segments.text: Today we are going to discuss binary search trees.
A binary search tree stores smaller values in the left subtree and larger values in the right subtree.
Searching takes time proportional to the height h of the tree, so the cost is O(h). For a balanced tree with n nodes, h is roughly log base 2 of n.
For example, if we insert 8, then 3, then 10 in that order, then 3 is the left child of 8 and 10 is the right child of 8.
